_meta.note: Contact points for legal process, mapped from infrastructure observed in a message. This file is a starting point maintained by the examiner. Providers change portals and addresses; confirm each entry against the provider's current published law-enforcement guidelines before sending process, then set last_verified.

process_tiers.basic_subscriber: Basic subscriber information (name, address, length of service, means of payment, IP at sign-up) - 18 U.S.C. 2703(c)(2), typically a subpoena.
process_tiers.transactional: Non-content transactional records (login IP history, session logs, recipient addresses, header information) - 18 U.S.C. 2703(d) court order.
process_tiers.content: Stored content (message bodies, attachments, drive files) - search warrant under 18 U.S.C. 2703(a)/(b); many providers require a warrant for all content regardless of age.
process_tiers.emergency: Most providers accept emergency disclosure requests under 18 U.S.C. 2702(b)(8)/(c)(4) where there is danger of death or serious physical injury.
process_tiers.foreign: Providers outside the United States generally require an MLAT request, a CLOUD Act agreement channel, or a request via the provider's designated law-enforcement portal. Preservation is still usually possible directly.

_meta.preservation_note: Send a preservation request under 18 U.S.C. 2703(f) as soon as an account, IP address or domain of interest is identified. It obliges the provider to preserve existing records for 90 days, renewable once for a further 90 days, and requires no court process. It does not authorise disclosure; follow it with the appropriate subpoena, 2703(d) order or warrant. State the account identifier, date range, and that the request is made under 2703(f).

providers.name: Google LLC
records_available: Subscriber information: name, recovery email/phone, sign-up IP and date, services used
Login and account-activity IP logs
Gmail header information (non-content) with a 2703(d) order
Gmail content, Drive files, Photos with a warrant
Google Workspace: often obtainable from the customer organisation directly
providers.notes: Requests are submitted through the Law Enforcement Request System (LERS). Preservation requests are accepted through the same portal.

providers.name: Microsoft Corporation
providers.jurisdiction: United States (Microsoft Corporation); Ireland for many EU accounts
records_available: Outlook.com/Hotmail/Live subscriber information and sign-up IP
Login IP history and connection records
Email content with a warrant
Microsoft 365 business tenants: request from the customer organisation first; Microsoft redirects to the enterprise customer where possible
Azure-hosted infrastructure: customer identity and payment details
providers.notes: Microsoft operates a dedicated Law Enforcement Request Portal for verified agencies; the report page links to the current guidelines and portal entry point.

providers.name: Yahoo Inc. (Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail)
records_available: Subscriber information, registration IP and date
Login IP logs (retention is limited; preserve early)
Email headers with a 2703(d) order; content with a warrant
providers.notes: Yahoo's Law Enforcement Response Team publishes its guidelines and submission channel on the transparency site. Yahoo IP log retention is short, so a 2703(f) letter should go out immediately.

providers.name: Apple Inc. (iCloud Mail)
records_available: Apple ID subscriber information, sign-up IP, associated devices
iCloud Mail logs and connection IPs
iCloud content (mail, backups, photos) with a warrant; end-to-end encrypted categories are not available
providers.notes: Apple's US guidelines document lists the accepted request formats and the law-enforcement email address. Agencies can register for Apple's law-enforcement support portal.

providers.name: Proton AG (Proton Mail)
records_available: Account creation date and, where retained, IP address of last login (only when required by Swiss authorities)
Recovery email address if set
Message content is end-to-end encrypted and not available
providers.notes: Foreign requests must go through Swiss authorities (MLAT or the Swiss Federal Office of Justice). Proton publishes its transparency report and process page; direct emergency contact details are on that page.

providers.name: Cloudflare, Inc.
records_available: Customer account information for a domain proxied through Cloudflare
Origin server IP address behind the proxy (with legal process)
Registrar records where Cloudflare is the registrar
providers.notes: A site whose A record resolves to Cloudflare space is being proxied; the real hosting provider is behind it. Cloudflare's trust hub describes its legal-process and abuse channels.

providers.name: Amazon Web Services
records_available: AWS customer account identity and payment details for a given IP/resource and time
Amazon SES sender identity and sending logs
Customer content only with a warrant and generally only if the customer cannot be approached
providers.notes: Include the exact IP, port where known, and timestamp with time zone; AWS addresses are reassigned frequently.

providers.name: DigitalOcean, LLC
records_available: Customer account identity, sign-up IP, payment information
Droplet (VPS) assignment history for an IP and time window
Server content with a warrant
providers.notes: Abuse address is for preservation and takedown; legal process channel is described in the guidelines.

providers.name: OVH Groupe SAS (OVHcloud)
providers.jurisdiction: France (OVH SAS); regional subsidiaries in US and Canada
records_available: Customer identity and billing for a server/IP
Server assignment history
Content requires French legal process or MLAT
providers.notes: For US-hosted resources OVH US (Virginia) may accept US process; otherwise route via MLAT / Europol / Interpol channels.

providers.name: Hetzner Online GmbH
records_available: Customer identity and payment for a server/IP
Content only through German legal process / MLAT
providers.notes: German hosting provider; preservation via abuse desk, disclosure via MLAT.

providers.name: GoDaddy.com, LLC
records_available: Registrant identity behind WHOIS privacy, payment details, registration IP
Hosting customer records for sites on GoDaddy hosting
Workspace/Microsoft 365-by-GoDaddy mailbox subscriber details
providers.notes: GoDaddy publishes separate subpoena and law-enforcement policies; domain records are held by GoDaddy even when the site is hosted elsewhere.

providers.name: Namecheap, Inc.
records_available: Registrant identity behind WhoisGuard/Withheld for Privacy, payment method, sign-up and login IPs
Private Email mailbox subscriber details
Hosting account details where Namecheap hosts the site
providers.notes: Very common registrar for lookalike phishing domains; privacy-protected WHOIS is the norm, so registrant identity requires process.

providers.name: Tucows / Enom / Hover
records_available: Registrant identity behind privacy service, payment details, registration IP
providers.notes: Tucows accepts requests through its legal-requests page; Canadian entity, US process may need a treaty channel for compelled disclosure.

providers.name: Zoho Corporation
providers.jurisdiction: United States (Zoho Corporation, Texas) and India
records_available: Organisation/admin subscriber details for a Zoho Mail domain
Login IP logs
Content with a warrant
providers.notes: Zoho Mail is frequently used for BEC (business email compromise) lookalike domains.

providers.name: Twilio SendGrid
records_available: Customer account identity and payment behind a sending sub-user
Message event logs (sends, opens, clicks) for the account
providers.notes: Bulk email service; the Return-Path or Received hostname identifies the account by numeric ID.

providers.name: Mailgun (Sinch)
records_available: Customer account identity and payment behind a sending domain
Message event logs
